title: America has 30 million single young men. Even Utah is feeling it | Institute for Family Studies
gist: Deseret News brief citing IFS: the US had 30.4 million single men ages 18-39 in 2025, up from 20.7 million in 2000, which IFS links to the young-adult happiness crash.

insights.claim: The US had 30.4 million single men ages 18-39 in 2025 versus 20.7 million in 2000, according to the Institute for Family Studies.
insights.speaker: Reagan Campbell (Deseret News)
insights.so_what: ~47% increase in single young men; implications for household formation, housing and consumption patterns.
insights.quote: in 2025 there were 30.4 million single men ages 18 to 39

insights.claim: IFS suggests the growing number of young men forgoing marriage may be contributing to the happiness crash among young American adults.
insights.speaker: Reagan Campbell (Deseret News)
insights.so_what: Links singlehood to wellbeing decline, a social-stability and political signal.
insights.quote: number of young men forgoing marriage could be adding to the happiness crash now unfolding among young adults across America
